narrative: Material PL2__M1136593 exhibits smooth daily demand (CV=0.44) with a mean of 14,324 units per working day and a right-skewed distribution. Lead times are unstable (CV=0.67, ranging 0.12–6.06 days), making lead-time variance the dominant driver of the safety stock requirement. A continuous-review (r,Q) policy is recommended: the EOQ of 43,401 units balances ordering and holding costs, while a safety stock of 25,092 units (z=1.645 at 95% service level) protects against demand-during-lead-time variability. Storage capacity is not binding at 49.4% utilisation.

research_insights.selection_rationale: Demand is smooth (CV=0.44) and largely continuous, making a classical (r,Q) policy appropriate. The EOQ formula provides a cost-optimal order quantity, and the reorder point is set to cover expected demand during lead time plus a safety buffer calibrated to the 95% service level. No intermittency or lumpiness was detected that would require a periodic or (s,S) policy.
